summary: # CLO Skills Workshop - Custom Button UV Mapping ## Overview In this workshop, we will explore the process of creating custom button UV maps using CLO software. We’ll go through the steps required to manipulate button textures and ensure they are applied correctly on garments. ## Introduction to the Button See this picture. It is a round button with two holes in the middle. We will focus on a specific type of button available in CLO, identified in the picture book window. ## Finding the Button 1. **Switch to List Display**: To find the button, switch to the list display. 2. **Locate the Button and Button Eye File**: Open the button file and find two round buttons that meet our needs. 3. **Display Icons**: Switch to display icons for easier navigation. - Hover the mouse over the button; a number will appear. For example, "A line button 9". Remember this number. ## Accessing the UV Document Folder 1. **Navigate to the UV Document Folder**: Go up to find the UV document folder and double-click to open it. 2. **Copy Document Path**: Right-click on the document and copy the path. Open the file and paste the path to access it. 3. **Standard PSD Files**: You will find many PSD files here, which are standard files that CLO has prepared for you. ## Preparing the UV Picture 1. **Open Photoshop**: Launch Photoshop and open "A line button 9". 2. **Review the Drawing**: Once opened, you will see the drawing divided into several areas with corresponding texts. - The largest area at the top represents the front of the button, while the bottom represents the back. - The upper right corner indicates the side of the button eye, with two small lines because there are two buttons. - Text is displayed in Chinese, English, and Korean; for our purposes, we will only keep Chinese. ## Adjusting the Layers 1. **Hide Unnecessary Text**: On the right layer, hide the English and Korean text, leaving only the Chinese text visible. 2. **Drag the Button Drawing**: Use the left mouse button to drag the button drawing onto the back layer. Adjust its size as necessary. 3. **Ensure Coverage**: Make sure the twisted picture covers the bottom green circle adequately. ## Layer Adjustments 1. **Blur Layer**: Right-click on the layer and select "Blur Layer" to refine the button. 2. **Adjust Vertical Lines**: Select the layer and press `CTRL + K` to adjust size, shape, and angle. Rotate it to a vertical state. 3. **Handle Eye Positioning**: Ensure that the eyes of the two lines match up correctly, as their size and position may not align perfectly. ## Filling the Selection 1. **Generate Selection**: Use the set tool to create a selection. Fill in other patterns using `Shift + F`. 2. **Repeat Fill Operation**: Select the content, identify it, and confirm. Repeat the operation with `Shift + F`. 3. **Copy Textures**: Copy the twist texture using `CTRL + C` and paste it with `CTRL + V`. ## Working with Side Textures 1. **Identify Side Textures**: The area shows both front and side textures. Magnify this area to get a better view. 2. **Adjust the Twist Texture**: If the texture is not large enough, adjust it using `CTRL + T` and the keyboard direction keys to match it accurately. 3. **Create the Side Circle**: Make a large circle and fill it with white. ## Finalizing the Texture 1. **Copy and Adjust Layers**: Copy the twist texture layer using `CTRL + J`. Use `CTRL + T` to adjust the size of the circle. 2. **Shrink the Layer**: Hold down the `CTRL` key while clicking the left mouse button to shrink the layer. 3. **Fill in White**: Use `Shift + F5` to fill in white on the sides of the twist. ## Saving the Final Image 1. **Hide Other Layers**: Before saving, hide other layers. 2. **Select Save Address**: Choose the save address and select JPG format. 3. **Quality Selection**: Choose the quality level required, preferably the highest level, and click confirm. ## Applying the New Twist 1. **Return to CLO Software**: Back in CLO, use the new twist we created. 2. **Add the Twist**: In the shape section, find the two-eyed round twist selected at the beginning. 3. **Update the Twist**: Click to add the picture just created. ## Final Adjustments 1. **Add Twist to Dress**: To see the twist effect, add it to the dress first. 2. **Select All Twists**: Use the move twist tool to select all five twists at the front. 3. **Rotate the Twist**: Ensure the purple part is above and the white part is below; rotate the twist 90 degrees counterclockwise. Change the angle in the property editor to 90. ## Conclusion This concludes our workshop on custom button UV mapping in CLO. Follow these steps to create and apply custom textures effectively.
